Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 35 November 1989 after 
the draft finali2ed by the Wool and Wool Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the 
Textile Division Council. 

Worsted lohis ( both all wool and blended v^ool/part wool with man-made fibres ) arc a widely 
used consumer item wjthin the country. 

It is hoped that the publication of this standard would ensure the availability of worsted lohis of 
desired quality to the consumers. 

For the purpose of de^jiding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, 
the final value, observed or calculated^ expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded 
off in accordance with IS 2: I960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values (rejisedy. The 
number of significant places retained \n the rounded off value should be the same as that of the 
specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard 
WORSTED LOHIS — SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements of 
worsted lohis 

2 REFERENCES 

2.1 The Indian Standards listed in Annex A are 
necessary adjuncts to this standard. 

3 TERMINOLOGY 

3.0 For the purpose of this standard, the fol- 
jowing definitions along with those given m 
IS 11206 : 1984 shall apply. 

3.1 Worsted Lohis 

Lohis made from virgin wool or their blends 
with man-made fibres spua on combed fibre 

spinning system. 

3.2 Worsted Span Yara 

Yarn spun from long wool fibre sHvers after 
rL;moval of short fibres on the rectilinear or 
noble comb and drawing through gill boxes. 

3.3 Worsted Blended Span Yarn 

Yarn spun from blended long fibre stivers after 
removal of short fibres in the combing process 



3.4 Virgin Wool 

Pure and new wool Commercially it means 
wool that has not been processed or used before 
and is thus distinctly diCfereat from re-processcd 
or re-used wool, 

4 MANUFACTURE 

4.1 Yarn used in the manufacture of lohis shall 
be spun from virgin wool or from the blends of 
wool and man-made fibres on combed fibre 
spinning system. The man-made fibres to be 
used for blending with wool and the blend com- 
position shall be as agreed to between the 
buyer and the seller. 

5 REQUIREMENTS 

5.1 Freedom from Defects 

The worsted lohis when visually examined both 
against light and on a flat surface shall be free 
from objectionable flaws. The objectionable 
flaws shall be those which strike immediately 
the eyes of the person examining the lohis and 
shall include: 

a) Missing ends and picks* 

b) Floats; 



c) Stains; 

d) Weft bars and warp section marks; 

e) Big slubs, knots and specks unless they 
arc a part of thQ design; 

f) Prominently noticeable thick and thin 
places; 

g) Cuts and holes; and 

h) Dyeing defects (streaks, patches, etc). 

5.2 The lohis shall meet the requirements as 

given in Table 1. 

5,2.1 Construction particulars of two popular 
varieties of lohis arc given m Annex B for 
information only. 

6 MARKING 

6.1 The lohjs shall he marked with the following: 

a) Name of the material, 

b) The words *A11 Wool', 'Blended Wool' or 
'Part Wool' as the case may be ( see 
NOTE ); 

c) Indication of the source of manufacturer; 

d) Year of manufacture; and 

e) Length and width- 

NOTE — In case of lohi3 ^ blended woal or part 
wool, the bknd composition shall al3t> be ladiCLiled 
in acL-ordanc-e wjrti IS 1793 : 19 73 

6.1.1 The lohis may also be marked with the 
Standard Mark. 

7 PACKING 



7.1 Bale Packing 

Each lohi shall be wrapped with low density 
polyethylene film of minimum 40 micron thick- 
ness and conforming to IS 2508 : 1984, A 
suitable number of such lohis shall ?gain be 
covered with another layer of polyethylene film 
of the same type followed by a waterproof 
packing paper conforming to IS 1398 ; 1982 and 
then be enclosed in an outer layer of hessian 
cloth/HDPE woven fabric, preferably conform- 
ing to Type I of IS 2818 (Part 2): 1971/ 
IS 6899 : 1984 in the form of a bale The bale 
shall then be strapped with metailic/synthetic 
straps. 

7.2 Case Packing 

Eac\ lohi shall be wrapped with low density 
polyethylene film of minimum 40 micron thick-* 
ness and conforming to IS 2508 : 1984. A suit- 
able number of such lohis shall then be covered 
with a layer of kraft paper preferably conform- 
ing to IS 1397 : 1967 followed by another layer 
of waterproof packing paper conforming to

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the pro- 
ducer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to 
that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from 
the Bureau of Indian Standards. 



BDreao of lodlan Standardi 

BIS is a statutory mstitutioti established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to 
promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality 
certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country.

any form without the prior permission in wrifmg of BIS. This does not preclude the free use» in 
the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or 
grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), BIS 

Revision of Indian Standards

are issued from time to time, Usery of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession 
of the latest amendments or edition. Comments on this Indian Standard may be sent to BIS
